business_problem: After merging three Islamic banks, BSI needed to modernize an on-premises information landscape that could not keep up with rising data volumes, risk calculations, and reporting demands while still meeting data residency requirements in Indonesia.
solution_summary: BSI moved its management information stack onto Oracle Autonomous Database on Exadata Cloud@Customer so it could keep the platform in its own data center while gaining autonomous operations and cloud-scale performance. Oracle Data Integration and Oracle Data Integrator automate ETL and change-data capture from Temenos and Microsoft SQL Server source systems into Oracle Autonomous Data Warehouse, which becomes the real-time reporting and analytics foundation for the merged bank. Oracle GoldenGate keeps source data synchronized, while the autonomous database layer removes manual tuning, backup, patching, and capacity-planning work from IT staff. This design gives BSI one governed platform for financial reporting, complex calculations, and future digital-application data stores, all while supporting Sharia-compliant banking services and customer-growth targets.
products_used: Oracle Autonomous Database on Exadata Cloud@Customer

data_flow: Temenos and Microsoft SQL Server source systems feed banking data through Oracle Data Integration, Oracle Data Integrator, and Oracle GoldenGate into Oracle Autonomous Data Warehouse on Exadata Cloud@Customer, where financial reports, risk calculations, and downstream digital-application data stores use the synchronized, governed dataset.
business_outcome: BSI completed its migration in four months, improved data processing and financial report production by 50%, reduced manual database administration, and created a governed real-time banking data platform that supports customer growth and future digital applications.
